To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the thermal profile of cryomilled compounds is a function of surface crystallization rates and the presence of a double exothermic peak in the DSC is indicative of the presence of a metastable phase.

1) the thermal profile upon heating is a function of the surface crystallization rate of the compound; 2) compounds that exhibit a high surface crystallization rate show a double exothermic peak in the DSC, whereas compounds that exhibit a low surface crystallization rate will exhibit a single exothermic peak.

The thermal behavior of cryomilled compounds depends upon the surface crystal growth rates around the glass transition temperature (Tg) of the material, with compounds exhibiting higher surface crystal growth rates showing a double crystallization exothermic peak in the differential scanning calorimetry profile upon heating.
